page: Vultr voc-c-8c-16gb-300s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 16 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. System memory consists of 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 300 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the top tier (top 10%) and Geekbench single-core scores in the strong tier (top 25%). Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range (middle 50%). Memory bandwidth tests, both cached and uncached, show average performance, with uncached read bandwidth at 118.62 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 68.98 GB/sec. Text processing is a relative strength, scoring in the top 25% on Geekbench, while medium (7B) LLM inference prompt processing is a relative bottleneck, registering in the weak tier (bottom 25%).

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers dedicated AMD EPYC compute resources and fast local NVMe storage without the premium of memory-optimized configurations, making it a balanced option for compute-bound workloads that require consistent CPU performance. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation make this server well-suited for workloads such as web serving, software compilation, text processing, and moderate database operations.
